## **2\. Literature Review**

### **2.1. CNN-based strong lens parameter estimation**

The application of CNNs to strong lens parameter estimation began with Hezaveh et al. (2017), who trained a CNN to predict SIE parameters (θ\_E, ellipticity, center) from simulated HST-like images. Perreault Levasseur et al. (2017) extended this to Bayesian neural networks for uncertainty quantification. Both works were sim-only; real-data validation was deferred.

Gawade et al. (2025) trained a CNN on HSC (Hyper Suprime-Cam) ground-based simulations, injecting lensed sources into real empty HSC cutouts—a recipe similar to our hybrid approach. On 182 real HSC lenses (SuGOHI sample), their CNN achieved θ\_E accuracy of 10–20%, bias \<5%, and an outlier fraction of \~10%. However, their ground truth came from their own YattaLens automated pipeline, not an independent spectroscopic benchmark—a circularity we address with the Bolton b\_SIE ground truth.

HOLISMOKES X (Schuldt et al. 2023\) compared a ResNet to traditional modeling on 31 real HSC lenses. They found a "very good match" for θ\_E ≳ 2″, but external shear predictions were poor (networks predicted values near zero), and no aggregate accuracy statistics were reported.

LEMON (Busillo et al. 2026\) is the closest published work to ours. Trained on 80k fully parametric Euclid VIS simulations (1–4 Sérsic sources, single-Sérsic lens light, SIE+shear), LEMON evaluated on:

* 60 Euclidised HST lenses (29 SLACS \+ 13 EELs \+ 5 COSMOS \+ 13 ACS, heterogeneous literature GT): θ\_E bias \-0.03″, RMSE 0.14″, NMAD 0.11″, R²=0.53 (Table 3).  
* 354 real Euclid Q1 lenses (success-filtered Walmsley \+ Rojas candidates, PyAutoLens SIE GT): θ\_E bias 0.01″, RMSE 0.17″, NMAD 0.07″, R²=0.71 (Fig. 12a).  
* Key limitations: LEMON uses fully parametric simulations (no real ingredients), performs no realism ablations, and admits degraded real-vs-sim performance (their Sect. 7). Per-lens predictions are not publicly available.

Cao et al. (2025) presented TinyLensGPU, a GPU-accelerated conventional modeling pipeline with nested sampling. Applied to 63 SLACS lenses, it achieved ≲5% deviation and \~10% catastrophic failures at \~3 min/lens—the closest conventional modeling reference. Their code is public, and per-lens θ\_E predictions were kindly provided by the authors for this work.

### **2.2. Domain adaptation for strong lensing**

Several works have explored domain adaptation (DA) for lens parameter estimation:

* Ćiprijanović et al. (2023): DANN+MMD for θ\_E regression, sim→sim (DES-noise targets).  
* Agarwal, Ćiprijanović & Nord (2025): MVE+UDA, sim→sim, \~2× target-domain gain.  
* Domain-Adaptive NPE (2024): UDA improves posterior coverage, sim→sim.

All three are sim-to-sim and explicitly defer real-data validation. Sim-to-real DA on real spectroscopic ground truth remains unclaimed—this is one of our contributions (though we find that DA does not improve over realism-calibrated simulations; see Sect. 5.4).

### **2.3. Positioning our work**

![][image1]

Our differentiators are:

1. Observational self-consistency (GEN4): The first CNN trained with real galaxies as both light and mass (σ\_v → θ\_E).  
2. Causal realism ablations: The first systematic decomposition of what closes the sim-to-real gap.  
3. Independent spectroscopic ground truth: Bolton b\_SIE, not pipeline-derived.  
4. Comprehensive real-lens validation: SLACS-62, S4TM-40, Euclid Q1-322, and Roman simulations—across HST, Euclid, and Roman domains.  
5. Domain-aware uncertainty: A NLL head whose σ correlates with real-world error (ρ=+0.71) and works as a practical confidence gate (confident-half fail 6%).

### **2.4. Roman status**

The Roman Space Telescope (scheduled for launch no earlier than 2026\) is expected to discover \~160,000 strong lenses (Wedig et al. 2025). Wedig et al. released public Roman simulations (Zenodo, 16,214 lenses) explicitly "to support … training neural networks"—but no Roman parameter-estimation network exists yet. Our instrument-agnostic generator, already validated on HST and Euclid, is directly applicable to Roman; we demonstrate zero-shot transfer fails (R²=0.11) and retraining succeeds (R²=0.93–0.94).
